text:
Emily (she/her): Hey team — quick Q. I'm planning to relocate from SF to Denver during my parental leave (due late May). How does that affect benefits, payroll, and the relocation stipend? Do I need to do anything before my leave starts?
Michelle (People Ops): Congrats! :tada: Short answer: yes, a few forms and timing matters. Can you share approximate move date + leave start date?
Emily (she/her): Thanks! Leave starts 2026-05-20, planning to move week of 2026-06-14 (so during leave). We have a small relocation stipend offered — can we still get it when on Leave? Also worried about health plan coverage and address for benefits mail.
Michelle (People Ops): Helpful — two threads: 1) Stipend eligibility & timing (finance + people-ops) 2) Benefits / address / payroll tax nexus. Typical flow: submit relocation request before move, flag that you'll be on LOA, we coordinate payroll/expense timing. For health insurance: coverage continues while on approved leave, but we need updated address in HRIS so carrier has correct info.
people-ops-bot: Please file the "Leave + Relocation" intake so we can route to Benefits and Payroll: https://redwoodinference.workplace/forms/leave-relocate
Emily (she/her): Got it — is there any tax withholding change if I move states while on leave? CO vs CA?
Michelle (People Ops): Yes — state tax withholding depends on your state of residence as of move date. Payroll needs a copy of the updated address BEFORE the paycheck that reflects the new withholding kicks in. If move date is after a payroll cutoff we may need manual adjustment. We'll tag Payroll for specifics once you file the intake.
Sam (eng manager): Also shout if you want help with project handoff. We should lock down on-call cover while you're out and while you're moving.
Emily (she/her): Would prefer to pause on-call during the move window — will be mostly offline.
Juan (eng): I can take on-call for the week of the move and help with the handoff. Happy to swap with someone later.
Michelle (People Ops): Amazing — thanks Juan. Emily can you paste a 2-line runbook for on-call in this thread and who owns which recurring tasks? Even a short checklist helps.
Emily (she/her): Sure — runbook snippet:```- Pager: route to eng-oncall (Juan week of 2026-06-14)
- Daily sync: skip standup for 2 days (notify team)
- Deploy approvals: delegate to Sam
- Customer escalations: notify Sam + Juan```
Juan (eng): LGTM. I'll add myself to rotation for that week.
Michelle (People Ops): Next steps from People Ops: 1) Emily files intake form (link above) 2) Update personal address in HRIS and attach proof if needed 3) People Ops will email Benefits & Payroll with timeline 4) We document stipend payment timing (expense vs payroll) and confirm tax treatment.
Emily (she/her): Filing form now. Thanks everyone. Appreciate the backup :heart:
people-ops-bot: Intake received (ID: RWD-LOA-3241). People Ops will follow up within 3 business days.
Michelle (People Ops): One more note — if you plan to travel back to CA temporarily during leave (e.g., to see provider), keep receipts and travel notes for stipend/expense reconciliation. We'll confirm allowable expenses.
Emily (she/her): Copy. Will keep receipts.
Sam (eng manager): Once People Ops confirms stipend timing I'll update the team calendar and ramp plan.
Michelle (People Ops): Great. We'll update you in this thread with any specific payroll asks. If anything changes to move date ping me directly.
Emily (she/her): Will do. Thanks all!
